summary:
Donald Trump rejected Iran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week and resume nuclear talks in exchange for lifting the US naval blockade of Iranian ports. Iran’s foreign minister said Tehran was still waiting for an official rejection and that negotiations were the only way to end the conflict. Russia and Ukraine also exchanged missile and drone strikes, with civilian deaths reported on both sides. The reported tolls differ: one account cited at least seven deaths, while another counted at least 16 over 24 hours.

Two mass shootings in South Africa killed at least 27 people, and police launched a manhunt for the gunmen. The attacks included shootings in townships in Cape Town and Johannesburg, as the country continues to face high levels of gang-related armed violence. In Bangkok, heavy rain flooded roads and led authorities to declare a disaster zone. Nearly 4,900 people were evacuated to shelters, and about 52,000 households were affected.

A suicide bomber struck a police checkpoint in northwestern Pakistan, killing at least 11 people and wounding about 30; the Pakistani Taliban claimed responsibility. A powerful storm brought heavy rain and strong winds to the northeastern United States, where hundreds of flights were canceled and tens of thousands lost power. In southwest England, police arrested several men on suspicion of explosives offences near RAF Fairford and evacuated homes while bomb disposal teams checked vehicles.

headlines.title: Trump rejects Iran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
headlines.summary: Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week and resume nuclear talks in exchange for lifting the US naval blockade of Iranian ports. Iran’s foreign minister said Tehran was waiting for an official rejection and that only negotiations could end the conflict.

headlines.title: Russia and Ukraine trade strikes, with civilian deaths reported
headlines.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged missile and drone strikes, killing civilians on both sides, according to their authorities. Reports put the death toll at seven or more in one account and at least 16 over 24 hours in another.

headlines.title: Two mass shootings in South Africa kill at least 27
headlines.summary: Gunmen killed at least 27 people in two mass shootings in South Africa, including attacks in townships in Cape Town and Johannesburg. Police launched a manhunt as the country faces high levels of gang-related armed violence.

headlines.title: Floods in Bangkok force thousands from their homes
headlines.summary: Heavy rain flooded parts of Bangkok, prompting authorities to declare a disaster zone and evacuate residents. Nearly 4,900 people were moved to shelters, while about 52,000 households were affected.

headlines.title: Suicide bombing at Pakistan checkpoint kills at least 11
headlines.summary: A suicide bomber drove an explosives-laden vehicle into a police checkpoint in northwestern Pakistan, killing at least 11 people. About 30 were wounded, and the Pakistani Taliban claimed responsibility.

headlines.title: Powerful storm disrupts travel and cuts power in US Northeast
headlines.summary: A powerful storm brought heavy rain and strong winds to the northeastern United States, disrupting flights and leaving tens of thousands without power. Hundreds of flights were canceled, and one person was reported killed.

headlines.title: Police arrest several men near UK air base used by US forces
headlines.summary: Police arrested several men on suspicion of explosives offences and evacuated homes near RAF Fairford in southwest England. Bomb disposal teams were checking vehicles at the scene.

headlines.title: Thousands protest Spain’s housing crisis after eviction
headlines.summary: Thousands rallied in Madrid after an 87-year-old woman was evicted from her home, demanding stronger tenant protections. Protesters called for measures to curb rising costs and evictions, including a ban on evicting tenants without alternative housing.
